meta.title: The Lantern on the Stair
meta.author: The engine test suite
meta.source: written for the engine tests; not a book anybody published

units.title: The Lamp Is Not Lit
units.caption: A narrow stair, and no light on it.
stanzas:
The stair was full of {gloom|near darkness}, and nobody had lit the lamp.
Mira put one foot on the lowest {tread|the flat part of a step} and stopped.
Above her the landing was still and black.

Her fingers found the lamp and {fumbled|handled clumsily} with the catch.
The glass was thin and {brittle|hard and easily broken}, so she went slowly.
Soot from last winter came away black on her thumb.
units.para: Nobody has lit the stair lamp for a long time. Mira climbs to it in the dark, finds the glass dirty and easy to break, and takes her time.
gloss: the flat floor at the top of a stair

units.title: Mira Finds the Wick
units.caption: A borrowed box of matches, and one short wick.
stanzas:
In the {watch house|a small hut where a guard sits} at the corner she begged a box of matches.
The old {wick|the cord in a lamp that burns} was short, but it was not finished yet.
She was {patient|willing to wait without complaining} with it, the way her mother had been.

Dry {tinder|dry stuff that catches fire quickly} first, then the flame would {kindle|to set alight} the rest.
It took four matches to kindle the wick at all.
For a moment the little lamp glimmered, and then it held.
units.para: She asks for matches at the corner and works on the stub of wick that is left. It takes four matches, and then the lamp stays alight.
gloss: shone with a faint unsteady light

units.title: The Neighbour Knocks
units.caption: A bolted door, and somebody on the other side of it.
stanzas:
Two nights later the lamp {flickered|burned unsteadily} and a {stranger|someone you have never met} knocked.
Mira had {bolted|fastened shut with a metal bar} the door out of habit.
She was {hesitant|slow to act because of doubt}, and she opened it anyway.

He had come on an {errand|a short trip made to do one job} from the far end of the street.
His voice was low and {courteous|polite in a careful way}.
He asked who had been lighting the lamp on the stair.
units.para: Two nights on, somebody knocks. Mira has locked the door out of habit; she is unsure, and she opens it anyway. The man wants to know who lights the lamp.

units.title: What the Lantern Was For
units.caption: One small flame, and a whole row of houses using it.
stanzas:
After that the lamp on the stair was a {beacon|a light that guides people} for the whole row.
Lighting it became a {custom|something people always do} nobody had agreed to.
Mira was {grateful|glad about a kindness done to you} in a way she could not explain.

Winter {dwindled|grew smaller and smaller} and the evenings grew long again.
The little flame stayed {steadfast|firm and not changing} on its shelf.
People still climbed the stair, and the light was still there.
units.para: The lamp stops belonging to Mira. Everybody on the row steers by it, nobody arranged that, and it goes on burning after the winter ends.

notes.title: Where this story came from
notes.caption: A page that is shown, not read aloud.
spoken: This part is shown between the readings, and it is never read aloud.
It exists so that the reader has something to teach that is not a scene.
Everything on this page was written for the test suite.
notes.html:
Not a real book

Every word of The Lantern on the Stair was written so that the reading engine could be tested against a book that is complete and belongs to nobody.

after.title: What happened afterwards
after.caption: A short page about the years after the story stops.
spoken: A lamp on a stair is a small thing to give.
The people who climbed the stair never learned who lit it.
That is the whole of what happens afterwards.
after.html:
Afterwards

The lamp went on being lit, and nobody on the row ever found out whose hand did it.

p1.watch: A dark stair, and a lamp nobody has lit. Watch what Mira does with her hands.
p1.focus: Listen for what she touches first, and for what stops her going faster.

debrief.ok: Yes — the glass. Thin glass is the reason she slows down.
debrief.no: Go back to the second stanza. Something in her hands is easy to break.

p1.writeIntro: Say what the dark stair is like, then give one detail from the text as evidence.

mc.q: Why does Mira move slowly once she has found the lamp?
opts: The stair is too narrow for her to hurry on.
The lamp glass is thin and brittle and could break.
She is listening for someone coming up behind her.
Her mother has told her never to touch the lamp.
mc.fb: The text says the glass was thin and brittle, so she went slowly. Nothing else on the stair is holding her back.

mc.q: What does the soot on Mira's thumb tell you about the lamp?
opts: It has been burning every night this week.
Somebody cleaned it earlier the same day.
It has not been lit or cleaned since last winter.
It has never been used at all.
mc.fb: The soot is from last winter, which means nobody has touched the lamp since then.

sa.q: What is the stair like before the lamp is lit? Use two details from the text.
sa.hint: One thing you can see, and one thing you can feel with your hands.

p2.watch: She has one wick and no money. Watch how many matches it takes.
p2.focus: Listen for the number, and for who taught her to wait.

debrief.ok: Four. Four matches for one small flame.
debrief.no: The number is in the second stanza, and it is not one.

p2.writeIntro: Give the number first, then say what it shows about her evening.

mc.q: How many matches does it take to kindle the wick?
opts: One, on the first try.
Two, because the first one blew out.
Four, one after another.
None, because the wick was already alight.
mc.fb: The text says it took four matches to kindle the wick at all.

mc.q: Where does Mira get the matches?
opts: She asks for them at the watch house on the corner.
She finds them on the landing beside the lamp.
The stranger at the door gives them to her.
She buys them from a shop at the end of the street.
mc.fb: She begs a box of matches in the watch house at the corner. The stranger has not arrived yet.

recap.label: Looking back — Act I
recap.q: By the end of the first act, what has Mira actually done?
opts: She has met the stranger and learned his name.
She has found an unlit lamp and got it burning again.
She has given up on the lamp and gone back inside.
She has bought a new lamp for the stair.
recap.fb: A dark stair, a brittle glass, a short wick and four matches. The stranger does not knock until the next act.
recap.wren: One lamp, four matches. That is the whole first act.

sa.q: Why does it matter that the wick was short but not finished?
sa.hint: Think about what she has, and about what she does not have.

p3.watch: Somebody is at the door. Watch what Mira does before she opens it.
p3.focus: Listen for the word that says she is not sure.

debrief.ok: Hesitant — and she opens the door anyway. Both things are true at once.
debrief.no: Read the third line again. She doubts, and then she acts.

p3.writeIntro: Say what she feels, then say what she does, and keep them in that order.

mc.q: What has Mira done to the door before the knock comes?
opts: She has left it standing open for the neighbours.
She has bolted it, the way she always does.
She has propped it with the lamp to keep it shut.
She has painted it and left it to dry.
mc.fb: She had bolted the door out of habit — which is why opening it is a decision rather than a reflex.

mc.q: Why has the stranger come to the door?
opts: To complain about the smoke from the lamp.
To ask who has been lighting the lamp on the stair.
To borrow matches for a lamp of his own.
To deliver a letter to Mira's mother.
mc.fb: He asks who had been lighting the lamp on the stair. He is on an errand, but that is not the question he asks.

sa.q: Mira is hesitant and she opens the door anyway. What does that tell you about her?
sa.hint: Being unsure and being brave are not opposites here.

p4.watch: The last part. Watch what the lamp has turned into.
p4.focus: Listen for the word that means a light other people steer by.

debrief.ok: A beacon. One lamp on one stair, and the whole row uses it.
debrief.no: It is in the first line of the last part, and the word is not lamp.

p4.writeIntro: Name what the lamp has become, then say who it is for now.

mc.q: What has the lamp become by the end of the story?
opts: A beacon that the whole row of houses steers by.
A nuisance that the neighbours want put out.
A private light that only Mira is allowed to use.
A signal that the watch house pays her to keep.
mc.fb: The lamp on the stair was a beacon for the whole row — it stopped being only hers the moment other people relied on it.

mc.q: Why does the story call the lighting a custom nobody had agreed to?
opts: Because the neighbours voted on it at a meeting.
Because Mira was paid to do it every evening.
Because it became a settled habit without anyone arranging it.
Because the watch house ordered her to keep it lit.
mc.fb: Nobody arranged it and nobody was asked. It simply became the thing that happened every evening.

recap.label: Looking back — Act II
recap.q: Across the second act, what changes about the lamp?
opts: It goes out for good and the stair is dark again.
It stops being Mira's lamp and becomes everybody's.
It is moved from the stair into the watch house.
It is replaced by a larger lamp the stranger brings.
recap.fb: A stranger knocks to ask who lights it, and by the last part the whole row steers by it. The lamp does not change; who it belongs to does.
recap.wren: Same lamp. Different owner. Nobody signed anything.

sa.q: Is Mira's lamp a small thing or a large one? Answer with what happens to the people on the stair.
sa.hint: There is no wrong answer here, but there has to be evidence in it.

notes.watch: A page between the readings. Nothing to do here but look.
notes.focus: Listen for who this book was written for.

debrief.ok: Right — for the reader itself, and not for a class.
debrief.no: The last line of the page says who it was written for.

notes.writeIntro: Say in one sentence what this page is for.

mc.q: Why is this page shown between the readings rather than read aloud?
opts: Because it is background material and not a scene of the story.
Because the recording for it was lost.
Because it is too long to be read in one sitting.
Because only teachers are allowed to see it.
mc.fb: It is background material. It is taught and asked about like everything else, and it has no lines to play.

mc.q: Who was this book written for?
opts: A class of students in their first year.
The reading software itself, so that it can be tested.
The people who lived on Mira's stair.
A publisher who asked for a winter story.
mc.fb: It was written for the test suite. Nothing in it is a real book, and that is the point of it.

sa.q: What is the difference between this page and a part of the story?
sa.hint: One of them is read aloud. Say what the other one is for.

after.watch: The last page. What happened after the story stopped.
after.focus: Listen for what the neighbours never found out.

debrief.ok: They never learned who lit it — and it kept being lit.
debrief.no: The middle line says what they never learned.

after.writeIntro: Say what the neighbours did not know, then say whether it mattered.

mc.q: What did the people who climbed the stair never learn?
opts: Which of them had bolted the door.
Who had been lighting the lamp.
How much the matches had cost.
Where the watch house had gone.
mc.fb: They never learned who lit it. The lamp was there every evening and the reason for it was not.

mc.q: What does this page add to the story?
opts: It names the stranger and explains his errand.
It says the lamp was put out soon afterwards.
It says the giving went on without anyone being thanked.
It says Mira moved away from the street.
mc.fb: The giving carries on, unthanked and unexplained. Nothing else on this page is in the story at all.

sa.q: Does it matter that nobody knew who lit the lamp? Say why.
sa.hint: Think about what thanks would have changed, and what it would not.

p2.label: Looking back — Act I
p2.q: By the end of the first act, what has Mira actually done?
opts: She has met the stranger and learned his name.
She has found an unlit lamp and got it burning again.
She has given up on the lamp and gone back inside.
She has bought a new lamp for the stair.
p2.fb: A dark stair, a brittle glass, a short wick and four matches. The stranger does not knock until the next act.
p2.wren: One lamp, four matches. That is the whole first act.

p4.label: Looking back — Act II
p4.q: Across the second act, what changes about the lamp?
opts: It goes out for good and the stair is dark again.
It stops being Mira's lamp and becomes everybody's.
It is moved from the stair into the watch house.
It is replaced by a larger lamp the stranger brings.
p4.fb: A stranger knocks to ask who lights it, and by the last part the whole row steers by it. The lamp does not change; who it belongs to does.
p4.wren: Same lamp. Different owner. Nobody signed anything.

guideVoice.name: Pip
guideVoice.hello: You found the door. Pick a reading and we will start.

passIntro.1: First time through you only watch. Nothing is marked.
passIntro.2: This time I point at one thing, and then I ask about it.
passIntro.3: Last one. You write, in your own words.

nudge: Close. Read the line once more.

end.1: That is the whole story. Now we go back through it slowly.
end.2: Good. Now the hard one: your own words.

p1.line: No light. Of course there is no light.

p2.line: One wick. That is all she has.

p3.line: Someone is knocking. At this hour.

p4.line: Still there. That is the whole point.

preshow.text: This is The Lantern on the Stair. It is short, and none of it is true.
Four parts, two of them dark and two of them less so.
Nothing to do in the first reading. Just watch.

p1.text: No lamp at all? On a stair?
None. Somebody stopped lighting it, and nobody started again.

p2.text: Four matches. I would have given up at two.
She had one wick and no second chance. That is why she was careful.

p3.text: She bolted the door and then opened it. Which is it?
Both. Being careful and being brave are not opposites.

p4.text: So the whole street uses her lamp now.
And none of them know whose it is. That is the ending.

notes.text: Wait — none of this is real?
None of it. It is here so the reader can be tested on something.

after.text: No. The lamp went on being lit anyway.

Explain in their own words why a character acts against their own hesitation.

Describe how a character changes across a narrative.

es: La escalera estaba llena de penumbra, y nadie había encendido la lámpara.
Mira puso un pie en el escalón más bajo y se detuvo.
Por encima de ella el rellano estaba inmóvil y negro.
Sus dedos encontraron la lámpara y buscaron torpemente el cierre.
El vidrio era fino y quebradizo, así que fue despacio.
El hollín del invierno pasado le quedó negro en el pulgar.
ko: 계단은 어둠으로 가득했고, 아무도 등불을 켜지 않았어요.
미라는 맨 아래 계단에 한 발을 올리고 멈췄어요.
그녀 위쪽 층계참은 고요하고 캄캄했어요.
손가락이 등불을 찾아 걸쇠를 서투르게 더듬었어요.
유리는 얇고 잘 깨져서, 그녀는 천천히 움직였어요.
지난 겨울의 그을음이 엄지손가락에 검게 묻어났어요.

es: En la garita de la esquina pidió una caja de cerillas.
La mecha vieja era corta, pero aún no estaba acabada.
Fue paciente con ella, como lo había sido su madre.
Primero la yesca seca, y luego la llama encendería lo demás.
Hicieron falta cuatro cerillas para encender la mecha.
Por un momento la lamparita brilló débilmente, y luego se mantuvo.
ko: 모퉁이 초소에서 그녀는 성냥 한 갑을 얻었어요.
낡은 심지는 짧았지만, 아직 다 타지는 않았어요.
그녀는 어머니가 그랬던 것처럼 참을성 있게 다뤘어요.
먼저 마른 불쏘시개, 그다음 불꽃이 나머지를 붙일 거예요.
심지에 불을 붙이는 데 성냥 네 개가 들었어요.
잠시 작은 등불이 희미하게 빛나더니, 이내 자리를 잡았어요.

es: Dos noches después la lámpara vaciló y un desconocido llamó a la puerta.
Mira había echado el cerrojo por costumbre.
Estaba dudosa, y aun así abrió.
Había venido con un recado desde el otro extremo de la calle.
Su voz era baja y cortés.
Preguntó quién había estado encendiendo la lámpara de la escalera.
ko: 이틀 밤 뒤 등불이 흔들렸고 낯선 사람이 문을 두드렸어요.
미라는 습관처럼 문에 빗장을 걸어 두었어요.
그녀는 망설였지만, 그래도 문을 열었어요.
그는 거리 저쪽 끝에서 심부름을 하러 왔어요.
그의 목소리는 낮고 정중했어요.
그는 누가 계단의 등불을 켜 왔는지 물었어요.

es: Después de eso la lámpara de la escalera fue un faro para toda la hilera de casas.
Encenderla se convirtió en una costumbre que nadie había acordado.
Mira estaba agradecida de un modo que no sabía explicar.
El invierno menguó y las tardes volvieron a alargarse.
La pequeña llama siguió firme en su repisa.
La gente seguía subiendo la escalera, y la luz seguía allí.
ko: 그 뒤로 계단의 등불은 동네 전체의 등대가 되었어요.
그것을 켜는 일은 아무도 약속하지 않은 관습이 되었어요.
미라는 설명할 수 없는 방식으로 고마웠어요.
겨울이 줄어들고 저녁은 다시 길어졌어요.
작은 불꽃은 선반 위에서 변함없이 타올랐어요.
사람들은 여전히 계단을 올랐고, 불빛은 여전히 거기 있었어요.

es: Esta parte se muestra entre las lecturas, y nunca se lee en voz alta.
Existe para que el lector tenga algo que enseñar que no sea una escena.
Todo lo que hay en esta página se escribió para las pruebas.
ko: 이 부분은 읽기 사이에 보여 주는 것이고, 소리 내어 읽지 않아요.
장면이 아닌 가르칠 거리를 리더에게 주려고 있는 거예요.
이 쪽에 있는 모든 것은 테스트를 위해 쓰였어요.

es: Una lámpara en una escalera es algo pequeño que dar.
Las personas que subían la escalera nunca supieron quién la encendía.
Eso es todo lo que ocurre después.
ko: 계단의 등불은 주기에 아주 작은 것이에요.
계단을 오르던 사람들은 누가 불을 켜는지 끝내 몰랐어요.
그 뒤에 일어난 일은 그게 전부예요.

This is The Lantern on the Stair. It is.es: Esto es La linterna de la escalera. Es corto, y nada de ello es cierto.
This is The Lantern on the Stair. It is.ko: 이건 «계단의 등불»이에요. 짧고, 하나도 실화가 아니에요.

Four parts, two of them dark and two of.es: Cuatro partes, dos oscuras y dos menos oscuras.
Four parts, two of them dark and two of.ko: 네 부분인데, 둘은 어둡고 둘은 덜 어두워요.

Nothing to do in the first reading. Just.es: Nada que hacer en la primera lectura. Solo mira.
Nothing to do in the first reading. Just.ko: 첫 번째 읽기에서는 할 일이 없어요. 그냥 보세요.

You found the door. Pick a reading and w.es: Encontraste la puerta. Elige una lectura y empezamos.
You found the door. Pick a reading and w.ko: 문을 찾았네요. 읽기를 하나 고르면 시작할게요.

First time through you only watch. Nothi.es: La primera vez solo miras. No se califica nada.

This time I point at one thing, and then.es: Esta vez señalo una cosa, y luego pregunto por ella.
This time I point at one thing, and then.ko: 이번에는 제가 한 가지를 짚고, 그것에 대해 물어볼게요.

Last one. You write, in your own words..es: La última. Escribes, con tus propias palabras.

No light. Of course there is no light..es: Sin luz. Cómo no, no hay luz.

One wick. That is all she has..es: Una mecha. Eso es todo lo que tiene.

Someone is knocking. At this hour..es: Alguien está llamando. A estas horas.

Still there. That is the whole point..es: Sigue ahí. De eso se trata.

None. Somebody stopped lighting it, and.es: Ninguna. Alguien dejó de encenderla, y nadie volvió a empezar.
None. Somebody stopped lighting it, and.ko: 네, 없어요. 누군가 켜기를 그만뒀고, 아무도 다시 시작하지 않았죠.

Four matches. I would have given up at t.es: Cuatro cerillas. Yo lo habría dejado a las dos.
Four matches. I would have given up at t.ko: 성냥 네 개라니. 저라면 두 개에서 포기했을 거예요.

She had one wick and no second chance. T.es: Tenía una mecha y ninguna segunda oportunidad. Por eso tuvo cuidado.
She had one wick and no second chance. T.ko: 심지 하나뿐이고 두 번째 기회는 없었어요. 그래서 조심한 거예요.

She bolted the door and then opened it..es: Echó el cerrojo y luego abrió. ¿En qué quedamos?
She bolted the door and then opened it..ko: 빗장을 걸고는 문을 열었네요. 어느 쪽이에요?

Both. Being careful and being brave are.es: Las dos cosas. Ser prudente y ser valiente no son opuestos.
Both. Being careful and being brave are.ko: 둘 다예요. 조심하는 것과 용감한 것은 반대말이 아니에요.

So the whole street uses her lamp now..es: Así que ahora toda la calle usa su lámpara.
So the whole street uses her lamp now..ko: 이제 온 거리가 그녀의 등불을 쓰는 거네요.

And none of them know whose it is. That.es: Y ninguno sabe de quién es. Ese es el final.
And none of them know whose it is. That.ko: 그런데 누구의 것인지는 아무도 몰라요. 그게 결말이에요.

None of it. It is here so the reader can.es: Nada. Está aquí para que el lector pueda probarse con algo.
None of it. It is here so the reader can.ko: 전부 아니에요. 리더를 시험할 무언가가 필요해서 있는 거예요.

Nobody ever thanked her..es: Nadie le dio las gracias nunca.

No. The lamp went on being lit anyway..es: No. Aun así, la lámpara siguió encendiéndose.

A dark stair, and a lamp nobody has lit..es: Una escalera oscura, y una lámpara que nadie ha encendido. Mira lo que hace ella con las manos.
A dark stair, and a lamp nobody has lit..ko: 어두운 계단, 아무도 켜지 않은 등불. 미라가 손으로 무엇을 하는지 보세요.

Listen for what she touches first, and f.es: Escucha qué toca primero, y qué le impide ir más deprisa.
Listen for what she touches first, and f.ko: 그녀가 무엇을 먼저 만지는지, 무엇이 그녀를 서두르지 못하게 하는지 들어 보세요.

She has one wick and no money. Watch how.es: Tiene una mecha y ningún dinero. Mira cuántas cerillas hacen falta.
She has one wick and no money. Watch how.ko: 심지 하나에 돈은 없어요. 성냥이 몇 개 드는지 보세요.

Listen for the number, and for who taugh.es: Escucha el número, y quién le enseñó a esperar.
Listen for the number, and for who taugh.ko: 숫자를 잘 듣고, 누가 그녀에게 기다리는 법을 가르쳤는지 들어 보세요.

Somebody is at the door. Watch what Mira.es: Alguien está en la puerta. Mira lo que hace ella antes de abrir.
Somebody is at the door. Watch what Mira.ko: 누가 문 앞에 있어요. 미라가 문을 열기 전에 무엇을 하는지 보세요.

Listen for the word that says she is not.es: Escucha la palabra que dice que no está segura.
Listen for the word that says she is not.ko: 그녀가 확신하지 못한다는 걸 알려 주는 낱말을 들어 보세요.

The last part. Watch what the lamp has t.es: La última parte. Mira en qué se ha convertido la lámpara.
The last part. Watch what the lamp has t.ko: 마지막 부분이에요. 등불이 무엇이 되었는지 보세요.

Listen for the word that means a light o.es: Escucha la palabra que significa una luz que guía a los demás.
Listen for the word that means a light o.ko: 다른 사람들이 길잡이로 삼는 불빛을 뜻하는 낱말을 들어 보세요.

A page between the readings. Nothing to.es: Una página entre las lecturas. Aquí no hay nada que hacer salvo mirar.
A page between the readings. Nothing to.ko: 읽기 사이의 한 쪽이에요. 여기서는 보는 것 말고 할 일이 없어요.

Listen for who this book was written for.es: Escucha para quién se escribió este libro.
Listen for who this book was written for.ko: 이 책이 누구를 위해 쓰였는지 들어 보세요.

The last page. What happened after the s.es: La última página. Lo que pasó cuando la historia se detuvo.
The last page. What happened after the s.ko: 마지막 쪽이에요. 이야기가 끝난 뒤에 무슨 일이 있었는지요.

Listen for what the neighbours never fou.es: Escucha lo que los vecinos nunca llegaron a saber.
Listen for what the neighbours never fou.ko: 이웃들이 끝내 알지 못한 것이 무엇인지 들어 보세요.
